thread.title: Apple, Intel Lift Dow To New High In Stock Market Today | Investor's Business Daily

author: NANCY GONDO
title: Apple, Intel Lift Dow To New High In Stock Market Today | Investor's Business Daily
text:
The stock market today showed mixed action as the Dow Jones industrial average hit a record high while the other key indexes headed south.
X The indexes opened lower, reversed higher, then pulled back later in the session. The Dow rose nearly 1% midday before closing with a 0.5% gain. The S&P 500 was fractionally lower, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq shed 0.5% as volume rose. Small caps sank for a second straight session as the Russell 2000 gave up 1%. On Monday, the index fell 1.4%.
Despite the overall tech weakness, several blue-chip techs fared well in the stock market today .
Intel ( INTC ) led the Dow with a nearly 4% jump, reclaiming its 50-day moving average in the process. Shares pulled back Monday as tech stocks were pressured. But they rose 3% Friday, after the chip giant reported progress in producing its next-generation chips . Intel is 16% off its high and may be building a cup-shaped base .

The true market leader also recovered all of its losses over the past three weeks. A Piper Jaffray report Monday said a bigger-than-expected percentage of likely iPhone buyers are interested in the higher-end iPhone XS or XS Max models. As a result, Piper Jaffray hiked its estimate for the iPhone average selling price to $770 (fiscal 2019) from $758.
Apple has advanced more than 20% from a 179.04 proper buy point it cleared on May 4, so investors could lock in some profits .
Paychex ( PAYX ) reversed from a sharp loss to close 1.4% higher after finding support at its 50-day line. Before the open, the human resources and benefits outsourcing company reported fiscal Q1 earnings and profit that topped views by a wide margin. Earnings per share rose 18% to 67 cents on 9% higher revenue of $862.8 million. Analysts expected 65 cents on $852 million in sales.
Gold miners, energy and utilities were among the biggest sector gainers, while apparel makers, retail and automakers lagged.
Stitch Fix ( SFIX ) plunged 35%, near a two-month low, as it gapped down below its 50-day line. Shares sank in after-hours trading Monday, after the online apparel retailer's adjusted earnings beat views but revenue missed . The Nov. 17 IPO had rallied as much as 250% from its offering price to its Sept. 18 high.
